label.description: Human-readable display name rendered in primary surfaces.

description.description: Supporting description used in detail and card contexts.

placeholder.description: Hint copy surfaced in form fields when the label is empty.

created_at.description: Timestamp recording when the entity was first created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for the most recent modification, when available.

last_event.description: Lifecycle event associated with the most recent timestamp mutation.

last_event_at.description: Timestamp for the lifecycle event captured in last_event.

classification_metadata.description: Operational metadata describing mode, storage model, governance rules, and audit timestamps.

categories.description: Ordered taxonomy nodes scoped to the object.

primary_category_id.description: Identifier of the canonical taxonomy node.

tags.description: Canonical tag collection after synonym collapse.

tag_count.description: Number of canonical tags assigned to the object.

tag_preview.description: Denormalized comma-delimited preview for list renders.

searchQuery.description: The current search query string entered by the user.

searchActive.description: Whether the search input is currently focused or has a non-empty query.

filters.description:
Array of available filter descriptors. Each entry defines a filterable dimension:
  - field: string (the schema field to filter on)
  - label: string (display label)
  - type: "select" | "multi-select" | "range" | "boolean" | "date-range"
  - options: array of { value, label } for select/multi-select types

activeFilters.description:
Array of currently applied filter values:
  - field: string (matches a filter descriptor field)
  - operator: "eq" | "in" | "range" | "gt" | "lt" | "between"
  - value: unknown (the selected filter value or values)

filterCount.description: Computed count of currently active filters.

pageSize.description: Number of items displayed per page.

totalItems.description: Total number of items across all pages. Used to compute total page count.

totalPages.description: Computed total number of pages (ceil(totalItems / pageSize)).

cluster_id.description: Hive's identifier for the cluster, an integer surrogate key declared as a string. Present on the entity lens; the semantic lens computes clusters on the fly and does not persist one.

lead_title.description: The title of the article that leads the conversation.

lens.description: Which clusterer produced this record. Not a detail: the two lenses answer different questions and disagree by design — entity is the persisted entity-and-title-token clusterer that the co-talker counts are built from, semantic is an on-the-fly pgvector cosine at threshold 0.80 that finds two people writing about one idea in different vocabulary. A cluster is only meaningful beside the lens that produced it.

member_count.description: How many articles are in the conversation.

member_people_count.description: How many distinct cohort members are in it — the number that makes a cluster worth reading, since Hive's default is the multi-person cluster its own signal uniquely produces.

dominant_category.description: The category most of its articles carry. Deliberately unconstrained: the server is authoritative and an unknown category is not coerced into the cohort's topic vocabulary, which is a different list serving a different purpose.

is_trending.description: Whether Hive marks the conversation as trending.

window_days.description: The lookback this record was read for. Every count here is only true of a window.

max_similarity.description: Semantic lens only: the strongest cosine similarity in the cluster. Absent on the entity lens, where it does not exist — absence means the lens did not produce it, never a similarity of zero.

mean_similarity.description: Semantic lens only, on the same terms.

people.description: The cohort members in the conversation, as {person_id, name, primary_topic, article_count_in_cluster}. primary_topic travels with each of them so a cluster that spans several slices of the cohort can be read without a second lookup.

members.description: The articles themselves, as {article_id, title, url, published_at, category, person_id, person_name}.
